transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My sleep has been completely off for weeks—either I’m up most of the night with my mind going or I crash and still wake up feeling worn out. It's really starting to catch up with me, and I just don't know what to do about it anymore.
Beyond your sleep issues, have you been feeling persistently sad, low, or lost interest in activities you usually enjoy over the past few weeks?

Yes, when my energy drops, a heavy gray cloud settles over me and I feel completely useless and guilty. I've also lost interest in things I used to love, like knitting, church, and volunteering at the food pantry. Lately, I just find myself staring at my yarn or ignoring texts from friends because it all feels so pointless.
Have you experienced similar periods of feeling this low, hopeless, or uninterested in the past, or is this the first time you have ever felt this way?

This is the first time I've ever felt this low and hopeless, as I'm usually a very steady person who sticks to my routines. These feelings, along with losing interest in my hobbies, only started about three months ago when the stress with my daughter moving back and my mom's health declining really hit all at once.
When you feel that the situation is pointless or feel like a burden, have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living or considered harming yourself?

Yes, there have been times, especially after a bad argument or when I mess up at work, where I catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn't wake up. I feel like my family would be better off without me, but I want to be clear that I haven't made any plans to actually hurt myself.
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have slowed down significantly, or have you found it nearly impossible to focus on simple daily tasks like reading or watching television?

I haven't really noticed my movements or speech slowing down—in fact, my husband usually complains that I'm talking way too fast. While my mind races or I sometimes just sit staring blankly when I'm feeling low, I haven't specifically noticed an inability to focus on things like TV or reading, so I'm not really sure about that.

When you are in these low periods, are you still able to manage your basic daily responsibilities, like preparing meals or keeping up with your personal hygiene, or have you become completely unable to function?

When my mood drops, it becomes incredibly hard to function, and my family has had to take over the household chores I used to manage. I even struggle with basic things like eating, either forgetting to eat all day or just picking at sweets and chips because I feel too drained to make a meal. I just feel so useless that keeping up with anything is too much.

To clarify the severity, have you experienced any periods where you have felt completely unable to function at all, or have you had any symptoms like seeing or hearing things that aren't there when your mood is at its absolute lowest?

Actually, those voices only happen when I'm in that wired, high-energy state, and they disappear completely when my mood crashes. As for functioning, I'm not completely paralyzed, but I've been written up for missing warehouse shifts, stopped volunteering, and my family has started tiptoeing around me and taking over my responsibilities.

You mentioned that you struggle with basic tasks and have missed work shifts; during these low periods, have you felt completely unable to function, or are you still able to manage some aspects of your daily life?

During those low periods, I feel almost completely shut down and walk around feeling useless, often just sitting and staring at my knitting yarn or ignoring texts from friends. I really can't manage much of anything, so my family has had to step in and take over the household tasks I used to handle. It feels like I'm barely functioning at all when I'm that low.
You mentioned hearing voices during high-energy states; have you ever experienced any delusions, such as believing you have special powers or that people are plotting against you, during those times?

When I'm in that high gear, I definitely get a feeling like I have a special gift for seeing how everything fits together, and I feel like I'm the only one who can fix all the problems because everyone else is just too slow. I don't ever feel like people are plotting against me, though. It's more just this really strong sense that I'm the only one capable of handling it all.

The presence of psychotic features during the mood episodes confirms a diagnosis of bipolar disorder with psychotic features.
